content_sections.heading: Eligibility Criteria
content_sections.text: Qualification: Post Graduation in HR, Marketing, Management or allied subjects from a recognised university with minimum 50% marks or equivalent grade. Experience: 3 or more years of relevant experience in placements, corporate relations, talent acquisition or business development, in a company, university, college or B-school. Other conditions: Demonstrable network with HR in hiring organisations. Excellent written and spoken English and Hindi; strong negotiation and presentation skills. Desirable: Experience of placements across commerce, management, economics, computer science and international management programmes. Experience in corporate training, student mentoring or alumni relations. Familiarity with NAAC/NIRF placement documentation; Delhi University or undergraduate college experience.

content_sections.heading: Who Cannot Apply for SGGSCC Recruitment 2026
content_sections.text: False claims or an unproven HR network lead to disqualification.

content_sections.heading: SGGSCC Placement Officer Job Description
content_sections.text: Placement operations: end-to-end ownership of drives, calendar, registrations, internships, offers and joining. Plan and run the annual placement and internship calendar: pre-placement talks, tests, group discussions, interviews, offer rollout and joining follow-up. Manage company onboarding, job descriptions, eligibility mapping, student registration and shortlisting for all eight programmes. Maintain accurate records of students, hiring organisations, internships, offers and placements, and prepare official logs and periodic reports for the Principal, Governing Body, University, NAAC and NIRF. Network with HR: build and sustain relationships with HR heads, talent acquisition teams and hiring managers across IT/tech, BFSI, consulting, analytics, FMCG, marketing, international business and allied sectors. Secure MoUs, internship tie-ups and repeat hiring partnerships, and negotiate competitive salary packages and roles. Collaboration with the Student Placement Team: guide, train and supervise the student team of the Placement Cell in outreach, event management, documentation and HR coordination. Set team goals, review progress and ensure continuity through structured handover between batches. Collaborate with Placement Cells of other DU colleges and the University. Alumni Engagement: build and capitalise on the alumni network for mentoring, referrals, internships, placements, and HR introductions. Closing the Academia-Industry Gap: meet regularly with students and Heads of Departments of all programmes to understand curriculum strengths and industry expectations. Use HR and employer feedback to identify skill gaps by programme, and recommend and conduct add-on courses, certifications, workshops and industry sessions, and present a gap analysis with an action plan to the Principal and department heads each year. Student Development: First Year to Final Placement: design and deliver a structured year-wise pipeline covering career awareness, aptitude, communication, resume and LinkedIn, GD and interview practice, certifications and internship readiness. Publish a documented internship and placement strategy with targets for each department.

content_sections.heading: Documents to Enclose
content_sections.text: Detailed CV One folder of self-attested certificates and evidence of experience and placements List (Names) of at least 10-15 hiring organisations you can bring to campus where you already have contacts Record of placements and internships delivered in the last 3 years with highest, median and average CTC and offer letters for highest CTC Documentary evidence such as MoUs, drive confirmations and HR testimonials Two professional references, including one from an HR leader in a hiring organisation
